smells.finding: Longest functions (compose_sector_predictions ~30 lines, score_sector ~25 lines) are short and single-purpose; size_calibration/assert_not_grossly_miscalibrated are a handful of lines each. No method approaches a length where intent blurs.

No behavior-bearing classes; only frozen (immutable, field-only) dataclasses (SegmentPrediction, ComposedSector, SectorComparison, CoverageResult, CalibrationSizing) plus one Exception subclass. All logic lives in free functions.

score_sector's two early-return branches (composed.uncomposable; official_time is None) both construct a mostly-None SectorComparison, which looks superficially repetitive, but each expresses a genuinely different null-reason (upstream uncomposable vs missing official time) via the same deliberate explicit-null pattern used throughout the module (no-frame-kill) -- not copy-paste-and-diverge logic duplication.

Functions operate on their own module's dataclasses; the only cross-module reach is predictive_t(composed.mu, composed.sigma, composed.n_eff, ...) -- the whole point of scoring a composed prediction, not envy of another module's internals.

The (mu, sigma, n_eff) triple recurs across SegmentPrediction and ComposedSector, but it is already reified as a named type at each level rather than passed loose as 3 parameters anywhere -- the data-clump smell's own prescribed fix (extract a type) is what was already done.

mu/sigma/n_eff/level are plain floats, matching the exact contract of the reused seam (src.common.student_t.predictive_t's own float-typed signature) -- a deliberate, consistent numeric convention at this boundary, not an unexplained proliferation of primitives standing in for missing domain concepts.

compose_sector_predictions takes 2 positional + 1 keyword-only (3 total); score_sector takes 2 positional + 3 keyword-only with defaults (5 total, 3 defaulted). Neither approaches a length that obscures the call site.

The frozen SECTOR_CALIB_* triple is consumed from exactly one seam (a single import block); a future change to those constants requires editing only frozen_constants.py, not multiple call sites in this module.

The module bundles 3 concerns behind clear banner-comment sections -- (a) position-sum composition, (b) Student-t scoring/coverage, (c) gross-miscalibration gating. Today each section changes for its own reason and the split is genuinely clean (independently tested, no cross-section coupling), so this is non-blocking; but as the instrument grows (e.g. a future gating rule or a second scoring metric), the file is a plausible future divergent-change magnet since all 3 concerns share one file. Worth watching, not worth splitting now -- the implement-result's own Workflow Feedback already explains the single-file choice was deliberate for a coherent Build-1 design.
No multi-hop attribute chains; accesses are one level deep (composed.mu, predictive.interval(level), coverage.empirical).

The injectable TailRule/FormulaRule seam is inherited from the already-justified student_t.py contract (passed through, not newly invented here). The sectors=(1,2,3) default parameter generalizes minimally beyond the fixed 3-FIA-sector case and is immediately exercised by test_uncomposable_sector_reported_explicitly_no_frame_kill (requesting a 4th sector) -- load-bearing, not a speculative unused hook.

The long module/function docstrings explain WHY (protected-intent no-leakback, Build-1 independence-sum honesty, owner ruling 5 non-Gaussian, no-frame-kill) rather than restating WHAT already-clear code does -- rationale documentation for genuinely non-obvious invariants, not a fog over unclear logic.
